script.vo01: There's an agent to guide financial services teams through these processes. It pulls data from The policy system and Claims history.
script.vo02: Before, they would have needed to jump across multiple systems to manually gather insights, piecing the picture together by hand, and hoping nothing moved while they worked.
script.vo03: It reads the policy system, Claims history. It engages you in Microsoft Teams and Outlook. And it can reconcile intercompany positions, showing the reasoning behind every answer.
script.vo04: Let's say a manager needs to reconcile intercompany positions. But what if the manager wants to go a step further? The agent handles the analysis and offers a set of targeted recommendations right in their workflow. Work like this used to require cross-referencing different systems by hand.
script.vo05: Now, with unified data context across The policy system and Claims history, the agent can rapidly generate a phased plan with quick wins. For risk mitigation, the agent helps as well, outlining a strategy that keeps the work on track. When the detail is needed, they simply ask, and the agent quickly compiles a clear summary.
script.vo06: It is explicit about what it did not read, so nobody mistakes a gap in the sources for a clean result. It names what it needs from a person before anything is written back, and who owns each step. And it says what would change its answer, which is the difference between a briefing you can act on and one you have to re-check. It can go further in the same conversation, without anyone switching tools.
script.vo_payoff: Finally, the agent creates a monitoring plan, so teams keep the effort aligned to the metrics they are measured on.
script.vo_helps: The result? Work that moves faster, stays consistent, and holds the same standard every time it runs.
script.vo_cta: Get started on your agentic journey today. Talk to your Microsoft representative to learn more.
